subject: Greenshore pilot: short top-up vs 3-week time extension — decision notes
messages:
From: Amit Singh <amit@greenshore.ai>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenshore.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot extension request — short top-up or 3-week add?

Hi Dev,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is seeing promising signal on entity extraction and the reduced token costs from your Optimize recommendations. We’re approaching the end of our 30-day pilot and wanted to discuss two possible paths forward while procurement finishes the PO paperwork:

1) Short top-up: purchase an extra 150k tokens (estimate attached usage) as a one-off voucher so we can complete the final integration tests (2–3 days).
2) Time extension: grant a 3-week timebox extension to the existing pilot (no immediate invoice), so our product team can validate throughput under heavier traffic.

High-level constraints: we need a path that doesn’t trigger a formal contract change on our side (procurement is slow), but still lets engineering run the final integration. If there’s a way to accept a small voucher or a temporary timebox without an SOW amendment, that would be ideal.

Can you share what Redwood has done in similar situations? Also please confirm whether the voucher would convert to a committed credit if we sign within 30 days.

Best,
Amit
Principal Product Manager
Greenshore Health

Attachments: greenshore_poc_usage.csv (CSV — sample token burn per endpoint)

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: Amit Singh <amit@greenshore.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot extension request — short top-up or 3-week add?

Amit —

Appreciate the clear options. Quick response from our side: both are feasible but have different operational and commercial implications. A quick summary to help you and procurement decide: 

- Voucher/top-up (150k tokens): fast to issue, shows as a one-time credit on your account, no contract amendment required. Tokens expire 90 days after issuance. Cannot be reclassified as committed spend retroactively, but we can apply good-faith credit toward first invoice if you convert to a paid plan within 30 days (we’ll document that in a short acknowledgment email).

- Timebox extension (3 weeks): we can extend the pilot window without changing the SOW, but our operational rule is that we need an internal ticket capturing the extension reason and the target deliverables. We typically require a short Annex (1 paragraph) to the SOW for audit purposes when we extend more than 7 days — that can be executed by email sign-off from an authorized Greenshore contact (procurement@greenshore.ai is fine).

Pros/cons: voucher = minimal paperwork, but no conversion guarantee; extension = cleaner for audits and lets you run heavier throughput tests (we can provision burst capacity during the extra weeks).

I’ve looped in Marissa (who handles commercial concession approvals) and Kimberly (legal) to confirm the exact wording we’d need for a minimal Annex if you go the timebox route.

Would you like us to issue the 150k token voucher today while we agree on extension language?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, Amit Singh <amit@greenshore.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot extension request — short top-up or 3-week add?

Amit / team —

Quick commercial note from our side: we’re comfortable issuing the 150k-token voucher today with these stipulations:
- Voucher valid for 90 days from issuance
- If Greenshore signs a paid contract within 30 days of voucher issuance, we will apply 50% of the voucher value as a first-invoice credit (non-refundable).
- Voucher cannot be split across accounts or transferred.

Alternatively, if you prefer a 3-week extension:
- We’ll provide the extension and enable burst capacity up to 2x for 72-hour windows during that period (subject to our fair-use policy).
- We’ll document the extension via a 1-paragraph Annex emailed by an authorized Greenshore procurement contact; no formal full SOW amendment required.

Operational ask: if you choose the extension route, please confirm 2–3 specific tests or success criteria (e.g., sustained 95th percentile latency < 400ms at 5rps/user, ingestion throughput X req/s). That helps our infra team provision appropriate burst.

I’ll approve the voucher issuance pending internal bookkeeping; Dev, please confirm the accounting code and we’ll cut it.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-minute call if you want to run through both options.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment (for internal): Greenshore_voucher_terms_stub.txt

From: Amit Singh <amit@greenshore.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenshore.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot extension request — short top-up or 3-week add?

Thanks all — after a quick sync with procurement, we want to take the voucher route to avoid delaying internal approvals. A few clarifying points so procurement can accept the email-based terms: 

- Please send the voucher and the short acknowledgment email that states the voucher is redeemable and that 50% may be credited to first invoice if we sign within 30 days.
- Can you confirm the token-to-dollar mapping you’ll use for the voucher? Procurement needs that for the PO.
- We also accept a follow-up Annex if we later need to document extension language (just in case).

If you send the voucher and the acknowledgment now, procurement will issue a small PO to cover the nominal processing fee so we can run the last tests this week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Amit
Principal Product Manager, Greenshore Health
